abda.title: Abda
abda.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
abda.note: Two men, and both only turn up in lists. One fathered Adoniram, the man Solomon put over the forced labour. The other was a Levite living in Jerusalem after the exile, and the parallel list calls that same man Obadiah.

abel-meholah.title: Abel-meholah
abel-meholah.note: A town in the Jordan Valley on the road the Midianites took when they ran from Gideon. It is also where Elisha came from: Elijah found him there behind a plough.

abiathar.title: Abiathar
abiathar.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
abiathar.note: He was the only priest to get out of Nob alive when Saul had the place killed, and he went straight to David and stayed his priest through the running years and the reign. At the end he backed Adonijah instead of Solomon, and Solomon sent him away from the priesthood rather than kill him.

abinadab-4.title: Abinadab
abinadab-4.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
abinadab-4.note: An officer from the united kingdom, named in a single verse.

abishag.title: Abishag
abishag.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
abishag.note: Brought in to keep the old king warm in his last days, and the record is careful to say nothing happened. The trouble came later: when Adonijah asked to marry her, Solomon read it as a move on the throne and had him killed.

abishalom.title: Abishalom
abishalom.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
abishalom.note: This is Absalom, David's third son. He killed his half-brother Amnon for raping their sister Tamar, and when David punished neither of them he spent years quietly building support before taking the throne by force. The revolt ended with his famous hair caught in an oak while he was still riding.

abner.title: Abner
abner.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
abner.note: Saul's cousin, and the commander of his army. When Saul died he did not stop: he kept the war going between David and what was left of Saul's house.

achish.title: Achish
achish.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
achish.note: He is the Philistine king of Gath, and he took David in while David was running from Saul.

adonijah.title: Adonijah
adonijah.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
adonijah.note: David's fourth son. With his older brothers dead, he was the presumed heir. He tried to have himself crowned while David was still dying, and left Solomon, Nathan and Benaiah off the invitation.

adoniram.title: Adoniram
adoniram.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
adoniram.note: Son of Abda, and the man in charge of forced labour under David, Solomon and, briefly, Rehoboam. He also goes by Adoram.

ahijah-6.title: Ahijah
ahijah-6.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahijah-6.note: A man from the united kingdom. 1 Kings names him once.

ahilud.title: Ahilud
ahilud.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahilud.note: Two of his sons served kings: Jehoshaphat was David's royal recorder, and Baana governed one of Solomon's twelve districts.

ahimaaz-2.title: Ahimaaz
ahimaaz-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimaaz-2.note: One of 3 men called Ahimaaz. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 1 Kings.

ahinadab.title: Ahinadab
ahinadab.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahinadab.note: Solomon put him over Mahanaim, east of the Jordan, one of twelve district officers who each supplied the royal household for one month a year.

ahishar-2.title: Ahishar
ahishar-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahishar-2.note: Solomon's steward, over the household in the list of high officers who ran the kingdom.

amasa.title: Amasa
amasa.about: Ishmaelite living at the time of United Monarchy
amasa.note: David's nephew. He led Absalom's rebel army, and afterwards David offered him command of the whole royal army to win back Absalom's supporters. Joab, jealous, stabbed him while pretending to greet him with a kiss.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

anathoth.title: Anathoth
anathoth.note: A priestly town in Benjamin, about three miles north of Jerusalem, and Jeremiah's home. He bought a field there as a sign of hope while announcing Jerusalem's fall. The site is identified with the village of Anata.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

argob.title: Argob
argob.note: A region of Bashan known for its sixty fortified cities, taken when Israel beat King Og.

aruboth.title: Aruboth
aruboth.note: Ben-hesed's district, one of the twelve that each fed Solomon's court for a month a year. It took in Socoh and seems to have lain in the grain country of Judah's Shephelah.

asher.title: Asher
asher.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
asher.note: Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe got a fertile coastal strip in the north, running toward Phoenicia, some of the richest land in Israel. Beyond its borders and city list little of the tribe's own history is recorded, and like Simeon it produced no judge or great hero.

azariah-11.title: Azariah
azariah-11.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
azariah-11.note: 1 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

azariah-6.title: Azariah
azariah-6.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
azariah-6.note: A priest from the united kingdom. 1 Kings and 1 Chronicles name him twice.

azzah.title: Azzah
azzah.note: Gaza, under a more literal spelling. The southernmost of the five chief Philistine cities, it sat on the coastal road between Egypt and Canaan.

baalath.title: Baalath
baalath.note: Dan was given this town, and Solomon later fortified it as one of his store cities. The name means mistress or lady.

baana.title: Baana
baana.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
baana.note: Solomon's district officer for the Megiddo and Taanach region, one of the men who supplied the royal household.

baana-2.title: Baana
baana-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
baana-2.note: One of Solomon's twelve district officers, over the country around Taanach and Megiddo.

bahurim.title: Bahurim
bahurim.note: A village east of Jerusalem, on the road down to the Jordan Valley. Shimei the Benjamite lived there. When David fled during Absalom's revolt, Shimei came out to curse him and throw stones.

barzillai.title: Barzillai
barzillai.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
barzillai.note: When David fled from Absalom, this old and wealthy Gileadite fed him and his men. David later offered him a place at court. Barzillai turned it down.

bashan.title: Bashan
bashan.note: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.

bashemath-3.title: Bashemath
bashemath-3.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
bashemath-3.note: One of 3 women called Bashemath. This one is a woman from the united kingdom, named once in 1 Kings.

bath-sheba.title: Bath-sheba
bath-sheba.about: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy
bath-sheba.note: She was Uriah the Hittite's wife. David saw her bathing, sent for her, and got her pregnant while Uriah was away fighting in David's own army. The cover-up ended with Uriah's death in battle, arranged by David.

bealoth.title: Bealoth
bealoth.note: Down in the far south of Judah, likely the same town as Baalath-beer. Solomon's list of districts also names a region Aloth or Bealoth under one of his twelve governors.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

benaiah.title: Benaiah
benaiah.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
benaiah.note: He commanded David's bodyguard, and before that he was known for killing a lion in a pit on a snowy day. He also beat an Egyptian giant by wrestling the giant's own spear off him and killing him with it.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

beth-horon.title: Beth-horon
beth-horon.note: Twin towns on the pass from the coastal plain up into the hill country. Joshua's army came this way chasing the Canaanite coalition in the battle where the sun stood still.

beth-shean.title: Beth-shean
beth-shean.note: After Saul died on Gilboa, the Philistines hung his body and his sons' bodies on the walls of this city. Beth-shean was Canaanite, in Manasseh's land. It stood where the Jezreel and Jordan valleys meet.

beth-shemesh.title: Beth-shemesh
beth-shemesh.note: It was a Levitical city on Judah's northern border, its name meaning house of the sun. When the Philistines sent the ark back, it came here first and was welcomed with sacrifice.

boaz-2.title: Boaz
boaz-2.note: Named twice, in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles, and nowhere else.

bul.title: Bul
bul.note: Eighth month, October into November, and Solomon finished the temple in it.

cabul.title: Cabul
cabul.note: Named once, in 1 Kings, and nowhere else.

calcol-2.title: Calcol
calcol-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
calcol-2.note: Known for his wisdom, and named with Ethan, Heman and Darda as wise men Solomon outdid.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

cherethims.title: Cherethims
cherethims.about: A military group in the Old Testament
cherethims.note: David's bodyguard, with the Pelethites, under Benaiah's command. They were tied closely to the Philistines and likely came from Crete.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

darda.title: Darda
darda.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
darda.note: Solomon's wisdom is measured against four famous wise men, and he is one of them. The name turns up again among the sons of Zerah.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling the largest territory Israel ever held, which Solomon then inherited. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

dekar.title: Dekar
dekar.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
dekar.note: Father of Ben-Dekar, one of Solomon's twelve district officers, whose region took in Shaalbim and Beth-shemesh.

dor.title: Dor
dor.note: A royal Canaanite port on the coast south of Mount Carmel. Joshua beat its king, but its people were never fully driven out, and it later went into one of Solomon's districts. Excavation at Tel Dor traces the shift from Canaanite to Phoenician on that coast.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

elah-4.title: Elah
elah-4.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
elah-4.note: His son Shimei ran Solomon's supply district in Benjamin. Different from the king and from the valley.

elath.title: Elath
elath.note: A port on the Gulf of Aqaba near Ezion-geber. Solomon held it, Edom took it back, Uzziah recovered it for Judah, and Syria finally got it. Modern Eilat keeps the name.

eli.title: Eli
eli.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
eli.note: The high priest and judge at Shiloh who raised Samuel after Hannah gave him to the Lord. His sons stole sacrificial meat and slept with the women serving at the tabernacle door, and Eli only scolded them. Both died in the battle where the ark was taken, and Eli fell backward off his seat at the news and broke his neck, aged ninety-eight.

elihoreph.title: Elihoreph
elihoreph.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
elihoreph.note: He and his brother Ahijah were Solomon's two scribes. Their father Shisha may be the man who was David's scribe under a slightly different spelling.

elon-bethhanan.title: Elon-bethhanan
elon-bethhanan.note: Joined with two towns of Dan to make one of Solomon's twelve supply districts, the one Ben-deker ran. Nothing more is recorded about it.

en-rogel.title: En-rogel
en-rogel.note: A spring just south of Jerusalem where the Kidron and Hinnom valleys meet. Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited there to carry news to David in Absalom's revolt, and Adonijah held his feast there to make himself king. Many put it at Bir Ayyub, Job's Well.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

ethan.title: Ethan
ethan.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ethan.note: In 1 Kings Ethan is one of the wise men Solomon outdid, and Psalm 89 is credited to Ethan the Ezrahite, possibly the same man. The name also turns up among the singers of Chronicles.

ethanim.title: Ethanim
ethanim.note: Seventh month in the Canaanite reckoning, September into October, and Solomon's temple was dedicated in it.

ezion-geber.title: Ezion-geber
ezion-geber.note: Solomon built his fleet here, at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba near Elath, to sail for Ophir, and Jehoshaphat's ships were wrecked here later. Nelson Glueck dug Tell el-Kheleifeh in the 1930s and called it the site, though later work on the pottery has kept the question open.

ezrahite.title: Ezrahite
ezrahite.about: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ezrahite.note: What Ethan and Heman are called. Both were wise men, counted as sons of Zerah in Chronicles, and the headings of Psalms 89 and 88 name them as the authors.

galilee.title: Galilee
galilee.note: Jesus grew up here and did most of his public work around the Sea of Galilee. Judeans thought the north provincial and mixed, which is the edge on Nathanael's question about whether anything good could come out of Nazareth.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

gazer.title: Gazer
gazer.note: The same city as Gezer. Pharaoh took it and gave it to his daughter when she married Solomon, and Solomon fortified it along with Hazor and Megiddo. The Gezer Calendar, a little tablet of farming seasons in early Hebrew script, was found there.

geber.title: Geber
geber.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
geber.note: Among Solomon's twelve district governors, each feeding the court for a month, two entries carry this name. The son of Geber was at Ramoth-gilead, and Geber son of Uri had Gilead itself, the old lands of Sihon and Og. Whether that is one man or two is unclear.

gera.title: Gera
gera.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
gera.note: He is only ever named as Shimei's father, and Shimei is the Benjamite who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion.

gibeon.title: Gibeon
gibeon.note: They tricked Joshua into a treaty by dressing as travellers from far away, the Hivites of this city northwest of Jerusalem, and so they lived but served at Israel's sanctuary. The tabernacle stood at Gibeon for years, and Solomon had his dream there. At el-Jib dozens of jar handles stamped with the name have settled where it was.

gihon.title: Gihon
gihon.note: Two waters carry the name. One is a river out of Eden that circles Cush and has never been matched to a known river. The other is Jerusalem's only natural spring, in the Kidron Valley, which Hezekiah ran underground into the city before Sennacherib's siege, and the tunnel can still be walked.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

gileadite.title: Gileadite
gileadite.note: Someone from Gilead, east of the Jordan, or of the clan named after Machir's son. Jephthah is the best known, the judge who beat the Ammonites and made the rash vow about his daughter.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. The personal name is the four Hebrew letters YHWH, printed LORD in small capitals in most English Bibles; Jehovah is a later hybrid of those letters with the vowels of another word.

haggith.title: Haggith
haggith.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
haggith.note: She was one of David's wives and Adonijah's mother, and her son tried to take the throne while David was dying.

hamath.title: Hamath
hamath.note: An Aramean capital on the Orontes in Upper Syria, the old northern limit of the land promised to Israel. Its king Toi was David's ally. Inscribed stones from the site, set up by a king the Assyrians called Irhuleni, were among the first Hieroglyphic Luwian texts European scholars saw, and reading his name gave them some of the script's first sign values.

hazor.title: Hazor
hazor.note: The head of all the Canaanite kingdoms, in Joshua's words, and the biggest city-state in the region. Its fall decided the northern campaign. The dig there found a huge Bronze Age city to match.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

heman-2.title: Heman
heman-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
heman-2.note: 1 Kings and Psalm name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

hepher-2.title: Hepher
hepher-2.note: Named twice, in Joshua and 1 Kings, and nowhere else.

hesed.title: Hesed
hesed.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
hesed.note: His son Ben-hesed was one of the twelve district officers who fed Solomon's household, a month each in turn, and Sochoh and the land of Hepher fell in that district. Of Hesed himself, nothing else is recorded.

hiram.title: Hiram
hiram.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
hiram.note: He was king of Tyre and a friend to both David and Solomon, sending cedar and craftsmen for David's palace and for the temple and keeping up the trade with Israel through both reigns.

hiram-2.title: Hiram
hiram-2.about: Syrian living at the time of United Monarchy
hiram-2.note: A bronzeworker, also called Huram-abi, sent by the king of Tyre to Solomon. He cast the temple's bronze pillars, the sea and the rest of the bronze furnishings.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hivite.title: Hivite
hivite.note: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

horeb.title: Horeb
horeb.note: Another name for Sinai, where Moses met God at the burning bush and Israel received the law, and where Elijah later ran and heard God in a still, small voice after the wind, earthquake and fire.

hushai.title: Hushai
hushai.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
hushai.note: David's friend, who stayed behind when Absalom rebelled so he could work from inside Absalom's court. Ahithophel gave Absalom sound advice, Hushai talked him into a worse plan, and the time it bought saved David.

iddo-6.title: Iddo
iddo-6.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
iddo-6.note: A man from the united kingdom, and 1 Kings is the only book that names him.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

issachar.title: Issachar
issachar.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
issachar.note: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.

jachin-3.title: Jachin
jachin-3.note: Named twice, in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles, and nowhere else.

jair.title: Jair
jair.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jair.note: He judged Israel twenty-two years. His thirty sons rode thirty donkeys and held thirty towns, which says money and reach, not battles won.

jehoiada-2.title: Jehoiada
jehoiada-2.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jehoiada-2.note: Known through his son, the commander of David's bodyguard who carried out the killings after David's death, in Samuel and Kings.

jehoshaphat-2.title: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat-2.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jehoshaphat-2.note: David's recorder, the official who kept the court's records, and he still held the post in the next reign.

jehoshaphat-4.title: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat-4.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
jehoshaphat-4.note: A man from the united kingdom, and 1 Kings is the only book that names him.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jether.title: Jether
jether.about: Ishmaelite living at the time of United Monarchy
jether.note: An Ishmaelite, by the record's own label, carrying a name several men shared. Exodus 4:18 uses it for Jethro, Moses's father-in-law, and Gideon's eldest son had it too, the boy too frightened to kill the captured Midianite kings.

jezreel.title: Jezreel
jezreel.note: A valley and town in northern Israel. Naboth's vineyard was there, the one Ahab and Jezebel stole, and it was there that Jehu wiped out Ahab's whole house. Hosea named one of his children Jezreel to say judgment was coming.

joab.title: Joab
joab.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
joab.note: David's nephew, and the commander of his army for most of the reign. He was loyal to what David needed rather than what David said: he arranged Uriah's death when asked, killed Absalom when told not to, and murdered Abner and Amasa under cover of friendship. David never forgave him. On David's word Solomon had Joab killed, even holding on to the altar.

jokmeam.title: Jokmeam
jokmeam.note: A Levitical town, probably in the Jordan valley near Ephraim's land, given with its pastures to the Kohathite Levites.

jonathan-2.title: Jonathan
jonathan-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
jonathan-2.note: A priest's son who ran messages to David from inside the city during his son's revolt, and once had to hide in a well to do it. He also brought word that a new king had been crowned.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kidron.title: Kidron
kidron.note: The valley along Jerusalem's east side, between the city and the Mount of Olives. Reforming kings dumped smashed idols and temple rubbish into it, and Jesus crossed it with his disciples on the way to Gethsemane the night he was arrested.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

maachah-10.title: Maachah
maachah-10.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
maachah-10.note: One of 10 men called Maachah. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 1 Kings.

mahanaim.title: Mahanaim
mahanaim.note: "Two camps." Jacob met the angels of God here near the Jabbok River on his way home, and split his household in two before facing Esau. After Saul died, Ishbosheth ruled the northern tribes from Mahanaim while David held Hebron, and years later David fled there himself from Absalom and heard there that his son was dead.

mahol.title: Mahol
mahol.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
mahol.note: Four wise men, Ethan, Heman, Chalcol and Darda, are called his sons in 1 Kings 4:31, and Solomon was wiser than all of them. The same men appear elsewhere as sons of Zerah of Judah, so "sons of Mahol" may be a guild or family name rather than a real father.

makaz.title: Makaz
makaz.note: Solomon had twelve officers feeding his household, and Ben-deker's district took in Makaz, Shaalbim and Beth-shemesh. That one verse is all there is, and the site has never been found.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

megiddo.title: Megiddo
megiddo.note: It guarded the pass into the Jezreel Valley. A Canaanite royal city, it went to Manasseh and Solomon rebuilt it as a chariot city. Deborah and Barak beat Sisera on its plain, and King Josiah died there facing Pharaoh Necho, a death mourned so deeply it became proverbial. Thutmose III's siege of it around 1457 BC is carved in detail on the walls of Karnak.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nathan.title: Nathan
nathan.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
nathan.note: The prophet who told David the story of the rich man who took a poor man's only lamb, let David condemn the man, and then turned it on him over Bathsheba and Uriah. Earlier he had brought God's promise that David's house would last forever. When David was dying, Nathan helped put Solomon on the throne ahead of a rival half-brother.

ner.title: Ner
ner.about: Saul's uncle living at the time of United Monarchy
ner.note: Father of Abner, Saul's army commander. Ner was Saul's grandfather or great-uncle, depending on how the genealogies are fitted together.

og.title: Og
og.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
og.note: King of Bashan and, in Deuteronomy, the last of the Rephaim, with a bed over thirteen feet long. Israel beat him and took his whole kingdom.

ophir.title: Ophir
ophir.note: It was the gold that made Ophir famous across the ancient world. Solomon's ships, sailing with Hiram of Tyre, brought it back in quantity, and the place itself was likely in southern Arabia or along the Red Sea.

paruah.title: Paruah
paruah.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
paruah.note: Father of Jehoshaphat, Solomon's district officer over Issachar.

pelethites.title: Pelethites
pelethites.note: They always come paired with the Cherethites, as David's personal guard under Benaiah. The names sound foreign, and they were probably hired soldiers of Philistine or Aegean background.

perizzite.title: Perizzite
perizzite.note: They come almost every time in a list, paired with the Canaanites, as one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel arrived.

pharaoh-3.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-3.note: Solomon married his daughter. Pharaoh is a title rather than a name, and the record never gives this one any other.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

ramoth-gilead.title: Ramoth-gilead
ramoth-gilead.note: A city of refuge in Gad's land east of the Jordan, and too useful for Israel and Aram to leave alone. Ahab died after being wounded there trying to take it back with Jehoshaphat.

rei.title: Rei
rei.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
rei.note: When Adonijah tried to take the throne near the end of David's reign, Rei stayed loyal, alongside Zadok, Nathan and Benaiah.

shaalabbin.title: Shaalabbin
shaalabbin.note: Allotted to Dan, but the Danites never fully took it, and Amorites held on there until they were put to forced labour. It is also spelled Shaalbim.

sheba.title: Sheba
sheba.note: The Queen of Sheba came a long way, probably from southern Arabia. She came to test Solomon with hard questions. She went home saying the reports she had heard did not tell the half of it.

shiloh.title: Shiloh
shiloh.note: The tabernacle stood at Shiloh, north of Bethel in Ephraim, for most of the time of the judges. Young Samuel served there. After the Philistines captured the ark, the place faded.

shimeah.title: Shimeah
shimeah.about: David's adversary living at the time of United Monarchy
shimeah.note: The man who came out cursing David as he fled Jerusalem, throwing stones and calling him a man of blood. He is from Saul's house, which is the point of it.

shimeah-6.title: Shimeah
shimeah-6.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
shimeah-6.note: One of 17 men called Shimeah. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named twice in 1 Kings.

shisha.title: Shisha
shisha.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
shisha.note: Father of Elihoreph and Ahijah, Solomon's two royal secretaries. He is likely the official called Shavsha under David.

shocho.title: Shocho
shocho.note: A town of Judah near the Valley of Elah, close to where David fought Goliath.

shunamite.title: Shunamite
shunamite.note: Someone from Shunem, a village in Issachar. Abishag, brought in to look after David in his old age, was one. So was the woman who took in Elisha and saw her son raised.

sihon.title: Sihon
sihon.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sihon.note: An Amorite king. Israel asked to pass through his land, and he attacked them instead. It cost him his kingdom east of the Jordan.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

succoth.title: Succoth
succoth.note: Jacob built shelters for his cattle here, east of the Jordan near the Jabbok, on his way back from Paddan-aram. The name means booths.

taanach.title: Taanach
taanach.note: A Canaanite royal city on the southwest edge of the Jezreel Valley, near Megiddo. Joshua beat its king, the town went to the Levites of Kohath, and its Canaanites were never driven out. Deborah's song puts a battle there by the waters of Megiddo.

tadmor.title: Tadmor
tadmor.note: It was Solomon's city out in the desert northeast of Damascus, on the caravan routes, and the Greeks and Romans knew it as Palmyra.

taphath.title: Taphath
taphath.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
taphath.note: Solomon's daughter, married to Ben-abinadab, one of the twelve officers who fed the court a month each.

tarshish.title: Tarshish
tarshish.note: Far to the west, at the edge of what Israel knew of the sea. Solomon's ships went there for gold, and ships of Tarshish came to mean any big ocean-going ship. Jonah boarded one at Joppa to get away from Nineveh.

tipsah.title: Tipsah
tipsah.note: Solomon's rule reached as far as Tipsah, a crossing on the Euphrates the Greeks called Thapsacus. Menahem sacked it when he seized Israel's throne because it would not open its gates to him.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

uri-2.title: Uri
uri-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
uri-2.note: 1 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

zabud.title: Zabud
zabud.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
zabud.note: Nathan the prophet's son, who held the title the king's friend at Solomon's court.

zadok.title: Zadok
zadok.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
zadok.note: The priest who stayed with David through Absalom's rebellion. He would have carried the ark out with the king, and David sent it back. Zadok anointed Solomon, and when Abiathar backed Adonijah and was sent away, Zadok was left as the only high priest.

zarthan.title: Zarthan
zarthan.note: The Jordan's waters piled up near Zarthan when Israel crossed on dry ground. Centuries later Solomon's bronze for the temple was cast in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarthan. Exactly where in the plain it stood is uncertain.

zeruiah.title: Zeruiah
zeruiah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
zeruiah.note: David's sister, the mother of Joab, Abishai and Asahel. David said the sons of Zeruiah were too much for him.

zif.title: Zif
zif.note: Second month, meaning brightness or blossoming, later called Iyar. It dates the start and the finish of Solomon's temple and nothing else.

zion.title: Zion
zion.note: The fortified hill on Jerusalem's southeastern ridge that David took from the Jebusites and called the city of David. He built his palace there. Archaeologists have uncovered the Stepped Stone Structure on that ridge, and many tie it to David's time.

zoheleth.title: Zoheleth
zoheleth.note: The serpent stone, by the spring of En-rogel outside Jerusalem. Adonijah held a sacrificial feast there to have himself proclaimed king while David was dying, and left Solomon and Nathan off the guest list.
